items.text: Why Are Financial Jobs Disappearing? Inside ADP’s Latest Employment Report
items.article: According to the latest ADP National Employment Report, private employers added 90,000 jobs in September. America's labor market continued adding jobs in September, but the gains were concentrated in a handful of industries. Meanwhile, some of the nation's most prominent white-collar sectors continued to shrink. According to the latest ADP National Employment Report, private employers added 90,000 jobs in September, which was a rebound from weaker hiring in August. But beneath the headline number, two traditionally higher-paying office sectors moved in the opposite direction: Financial activities lost 16,000 jobs and professional and business services shed 11,000 positions. The new data has shown a growing divide in the labor market. While hiring remains healthy in areas like healthcare, education and hospitality, many office-based industries are grappling with slower demand and artificial intelligence taking over prior job functions Due to this, college graduates and young professionals are facing one of the most challenging white-collar job markets in years, experts say. “The easiest answer would be AI and the disappearance of entry level jobs in the financial sector, but it may be deeper than that,” Kevin Thompson, CEO of 9i Capital Group and host of the 9innings podcast, told Newsweek . “The real answer probably lies somewhere between AI and interest rates. With higher interest rates comes reduced financial activity.”

items.article: A video released by the prime minister's office showed Netanyahu embracing the passenger and praising his actions during the emergency. Flydubai passenger Yaniv Hayun, who barged into the cockpit and restrained the attacker, met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday and recounted how he helped during the mid-air emergency, the Times of Israel reported. Hayun said watching the documentary series ‘Air Crash Investigation’ helped him understand what to do during the crisis. He also told Netanyahu that he pulled back on the aircraft’s controls after the attacker had been subdued. When Netanyahu asked, “You pulled them?" Hayun replied: “Yes, I watch ‘ Air Crash Investigation .’" The Canadian documentary series, also known internationally as Mayday, first aired in 2003 and is produced by Cineflix Productions. It examines major aviation accidents and the investigations into their causes through dramatic reconstructions, interviews and computer-generated animations depicting events inside cockpits and passenger cabins. Hayun was among the passengers who intervened after an alleged attack inside the cockpit during a Flydubai flight travelling from the United Arab Emirates to Israel. One pilot was reportedly stabbed by another, who then allegedly attempted to crash the aircraft. The aircraft reportedly lost roughly half its altitude in about a minute, prompting passengers and a crew member to force their way into the cockpit.

items.article: Even when a gift is not taxable, maintaining a basic record can be useful, particularly for substantial cash gifts or valuable assets. A viral discussion around a bride receiving wedding gifts worth Rs 10 lakh has raised a very practical question: does the recipient have to pay tax on such gifts? The answer is not simply about how big the gift amount is. The occasion and the nature of the gift matter. Under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act, certain gifts received without consideration can become taxable. If money received as a gift from non-relatives crosses Rs 50,000 in a financial year, the entire amount, and not merely the amount above Rs 50,000, can generally be treated as taxable income.
